world.summary: Added four hidden final-island sockets to the slice sea. One 5x5 dockless islet is sketched at x41-45, y11-15 with its claim tile at 43,16, and the mirror gives the other three: 65,11 (claim 67,16), 41,95 (claim 43,94) and 65,95 (claim 67,94). Two sit in the north-centre sector and two in the south-centre one. The pipeline has final-socket rectangles with claimX/claimY in the Tiled objects layer. They reach SeaMapSource.finalSockets (optional, so the other lanes' literal maps still compile) and SeaMapDefinition.finalSockets (defaults to []). seaMap.ts gains TileRect, FinalSocket, SECTOR_GRID, sectorOf (floor(3x/width), floor(3y/height)) and chooseFinalSocket(map, secret), which runs the murmur3 fmix32 Math.imul finaliser and then takes the value modulo the socket count. seaValidation.ts counts socket land as owned and names a dock inside a socket. The new validateFinalSockets, called from validateSeaMap, checks shape, sector pairs, the 90 s reach from every spawn, at least 12 navigable tiles in each circle, and 8 tiles of clearance from keepClearZones (hub, spawns, docks, 14 tiles out from each dock, the out-of-sight row). build-map prints each socket's sector, worst spawn time and circle count: every socket is 34.102 s from its farthest spawn with 35 navigable tiles in its circle. Tests in maps.test.ts cover the converter, the regular map being unchanged, the socket structure and mirror, the sector grid, the failing synthetic maps, and the selection (determinism, RangeErrors, uniformity within 5% over 30,000 secrets for three secret patterns). The unchanged-map test uses FNV-1a checksum 0x380609a9 of the old rows, computed from the pre-edit sliceSea.ts. Docs updated. Checks run in this worktree after npm ci: npm run typecheck (exit 0), npm run test:unit (36 files, 855 tests passed), npm run test:integration (6 files, 38 tests passed), npm run build (exit 0, smoke passed), npm run map:check (up to date). Playwright was not run. Nothing committed.
open_assumptions: The task says map.docks holds 16 docks, but the pre-edit map has 8. The test asserts that those same 8 docks, in the same order, are unchanged.
The keep-clear route covers the 14 tiles straight out from every dock, a superset of the sail-and-dock route south of Palm Key's south dock, so the mirrored equivalents are protected too.
A socket's sector is the sector of its claim tile. For the slice's sockets, the islet rectangle lies in the same sector.
The murmur3 finaliser permutes the 32-bit integers; it is a mixer, not a one-way function, so the secrecy rests entirely on the server's cryptographic secret. The docs say so.
Sockets carry no theme. The web client draws land outside every island with the tropical theme, so the four islets look alike.
SeaMapRules gained a required finalSockets count (4 for the slice); no code outside the owned files constructs SeaMapRules.
The architecture doc's open-sea figure changed from 91 % to 90 % (90.1 % with the islets).
